items.title: Warning issued about Eventbrite listings falsely using City of Mississauga’s name
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is warning residents after two Eventbrite listings were found with false claims. The city became aware of the two Eventbrite listings for the International Conference on Leadership, Innovation, Global Investment, & Professional Development (ICLIGP), the city said in a press release. The listings falsely claim to be in partnership with the city and state that the event will take place at Malton Community Centre from Aug. 31 to Sept. 2 and Nov. 30, the city said. “The City is not affiliated with these events, and no booking exists for this at any City facility,” the city said. ” The city urged residents and businesses to verify event details before registering or purchasing tickets. One event was deleted from Eventbrite as of Monday. An event listed on Eventbrite claimed to be associated with the City of Mississauga.

items.title: This Mississauga mom had her skin cancer symptoms dismissed by dermatologists. A new clinic came to the rescue
items.summary: Liliya Leheta had a referral declined. A new program at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre diagnosed her within two weeks. Liliya Leheta at her Mississauga home. The mother of three and nail salon owner discovered a strange mole on her chest that continued to grow over time. But her symptoms were dismissed by dermatologists, and her referral to a specialist was declined. Liliya Leheta, a Mississauga-based mom of three, was out with her kids on a sunny day in March of 2023 when she realized she forgot to apply sunscreen. The next day, she noticed her skin peeling on her sternum, but thought little of it — until, less than a year later, she noticed a strange, red mole that suddenly appeared near the centre of her chest. A striking shift in demographics is worrying doctors who say it’s part of a wider trend showing steep increases of cancer in people under 50. A striking shift in demographics is worrying doctors who say it’s part of a wider trend showing steep increases of cancer in people under 50. Over the next two years, Leheta would watch in horror as the tiny red dot swelled, changed shape and bled. ” Then, in the fall of 2025, Leheta learned of a recently opened rapid assessment centre for skin cancer at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre. Within two weeks of her referral, she was seen and diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma — the most common form of skin cancer in Canada. Less than two months later, a surgeon successfully removed the cancerous tissue. Leheta remains cancer-free to this day.

items.title: Georgia Attard (Gina)
items.summary: It is with great sadness that we regret to announce the passing of our mother, Georgia (Gina) Attard (nee Borg). Georgia passed away at the age of 86 at Chatham-Kent Hospice on August 3, 2026. Georgia was born in Malta to Anna and Andrew Borg on February 11, 1940. In 1958, travelling alone, she moved to Canada. Georgia is survived by her three children, Rick (Brenda), Brian (Sandie), and Sharon Guillou; her four grandchildren, Lindsay Guillou (Ben), Wesley (Carrie), Jessica (Ryan), and Amber Attard (Austin); her brother, Fred; and her sisters, Josie and Bessie. She had many cousins, nieces, nephews, and numerous friends. Special thanks to the staff at Blenheim Village Long Term Care, Chatham Hospital, and Chatham-Kent Hospice for caring for Georgia for the past seven months. Georgia came to Toronto, Ontario, and was a long-time resident of Streetsville, Georgetown, and Barrie, finally residing in Blenheim, Ontario. She will be missed more than words can express.

items.title: After Years of Disruption, an LRT Train Is Finally Set to Roll Down Topflight Drive
items.summary: According to INsauga, Ontario Transportation Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria announced Friday that a Hazel McCallion Line light rail vehicle is set to begin testing on Topflight Drive in Mississauga next week, following years of construction, delays and road disruptions tied to the project. Sarkaria shared the update in a post on X, saying progress continues on the line, though he did not offer further details on how long the testing would run or how far the train would travel. INsauga reports the significance of this round of testing is that it will happen on the actual LRT corridor itself, rather than being confined to the project's operations, maintenance and storage facility near Highway 407. That facility was the site of an earlier milestone, when Metrolinx said in June that the outdoor rail yard's overhead catenary system had been energized, allowing one of the project's light rail vehicles to operate under its own power for the first time. Metrolinx said at the time that achievement would pave the way for testing vehicles on the line itself, which now appears to be happening. For residents who have lived alongside years of construction along the corridor, next week's test marks one of the first visible signs of trains actually running on Mississauga streets.

items.title: Mississauga marks 200th anniversary of one of Ontario’s oldest log houses Aug. 8
items.summary: The Leslie Log House, built in 1826 by Scottish settlers, is one of Ontario’s oldest surviving log homes — and Mississauga is throwing it a free party. The Leslie Log House is operated by the Streetsville Historical Society. One of Ontario’s oldest surviving log homes is celebrating 200 years this weekend in Mississauga. The City of Mississauga and Streetsville Historical Society are hosting a public event to mark two centuries of the Leslie Log House on Aug. 8, according to a city press release. Built in 1826, the house was first occupied by John Leslie Sr. and his wife Esther Beattie Leslie, who arrived in Upper Canada (modern-day Ontario) from Scotland in 1824. m. Originally located near Derry Road and Mississauga Road in Meadowvale, the house was relocated to 4415 Mississauga Rd. in 1994 for preservation. It was designated under the Ontario Heritage Act for its architectural, historical and cultural significance.

items.title: City launches $25 adoption event as animal shelter reaches capacity
items.summary: The Homeward Bound adoption event offers $25 adoption fees for all dogs and cats from August 8 to 22. Are you looking to add a furry family member to your home? Now is the perfect time to adopt one. The Mississauga Animal Services Shelter is asking residents to help shelter animals find loving homes during the Homeward Bound adoption event. With the shelter reaching capacity for dogs, every adoption helps create space for other animals in need. From August 8 to 22, all dogs and cats at the shelter can be adopted for just $25, plus HST and any applicable pet licence fees for Mississauga residents. This reduced adoption fee offers significant savings compared to regular fees, which are typically $280 plus HST for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus HST for cats and kittens. items.title: Two wanted after allegedly posing as landlords and tenants in $30K Mississauga rental scam
items.summary: Police said victims would visit the unit being listed online and pay to secure it. But when they later arrived to move in, the unit wouldn’t be available. Peel police issued two arrest warrants for individuals who are based in Canada’s west coast. Two people are wanted after they posed as landlords and tenants to swindle more than $30,000 from at least eight prospective renters in Mississauga, Peel police say. Police said that between January and February of last year, the suspects would advertise rental opportunities through social media. When victims visited the listed apartment, they met with people who posed as current tenants and ended up signing rental agreements online. The victims were asked to pay by e-transfer to secure the unit, according to police, but upon arriving to take occupancy, they would discover the unit was no longer available. The person who was posing as the landlord would also be unreachable. Toronto police investigators say they have to adapt to a new reality, one dominated by “Investigators have identified at least eight victims with combined financial losses exceeding $30,000,” police said in a release. C. They are wanted for fraud exceeding $5,000.
